question:
Which element was arbitrarily assigned a value of 4.0 in the ‘Halogens’ section in 1922 by Linus Pauling, an American scientist?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Fluorine
Iodine
Astatine
Bromine
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fluorine

Explanation:
In 1922, American scientist Linus Pauling assigned arbitrary electronegativity values to elements in the 'Halogens' group. He assigned Fluorine (F) a value of 4.0, which was the highest electronegativity value at that time. Electronegativity represents an element's ability to attract electrons towards itself. The electronegativity values of other halogens (chlorine, bromine, iodine) were determined relative to fluorine. Fluorine's value remains valid today, and it is the most electronegative element in the periodic table.

Extra Facts:
Halogen group elements (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine) are highly reactive and do not occur freely in nature. They form salts with metals. Fluorine is used in toothpaste, plastics (Teflon), and nuclear energy. Pauling developed the concept of electronegativity and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954 for his contributions.

question_hi:
1922 में अमेरिकी वैज्ञानिक लीनियस पॉलिंग द्वारा 'हैलोजन' खंड में किस तत्व को स्वैच्छिक रूप से 4.0 का मान दिया गया था ?

[SSC CGL 2023]

आयोडीन
ऐस्टेटीन
ब्रोमीन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है फ्लोरीन

Explanation:
1922 में, अमेरिकी वैज्ञानिक लीनियस पॉलिंग ने 'हैलोजन' समूह के तत्वों के लिए इलेक्ट्रोनगेटिविटी मान निर्धारित किए। उन्होंने फ्लोरीन (F) को स्वैच्छिक रूप से 4.0 का मान दिया, जो उस समय सबसे अधिक इलेक्ट्रोनगेटिविटी मान था। इलेक्ट्रोनगेटिविटी किसी तत्व की इलेक्ट्रॉनों को अपनी ओर आकर्षित करने की क्षमता को दर्शाती है। फ्लोरीन के बाद अन्य हैलोजन तत्वों (क्लोरीन, ब्रोमीन, आयोडीन) के इलेक्ट्रोनगेटिविटी मान इसी के आधार पर निर्धारित किए गए। फ्लोरीन का यह मान आज भी मान्य है और यह आवर्त सारणी में सबसे अधिक इलेक्ट्रोनगेटिव तत्व है।

Extra Facts:
हैलोजन समूह के तत्व (फ्लोरीन, क्लोरीन, ब्रोमीन, आयोडीन, ऐस्टेटीन) अत्यधिक प्रतिक्रियाशील होते हैं और प्रकृति में मुक्त अवस्था में नहीं पाए जाते। ये धातुओं के साथ मिलकर लवण बनाते हैं। फ्लोरीन का उपयोग टूथपेस्ट, प्लास्टिक (टेफ्लॉन), और परमाणु ऊर्जा में किया जाता है। पॉलिंग ने इलेक्ट्रोनगेटिविटी की अवधारणा को विकसित किया और इसके लिए 1954 में रसायन विज्ञान में नोबेल पुरस्कार प्राप्त किया।

question:
Which of the following elements is a member of the actinide series?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Lutetium
Thorium
Magnesium
Lanthanum
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Thorium

Explanation:
The actinide series includes elements with atomic numbers from 89 (Actinium) to 103 (Lawrencium), where the 5f orbitals are being filled. Thorium (Th) has an atomic number of 90, making it a member of the actinide series. The other options, Lutetium (Lu) and Lanthanum (La), belong to the lanthanide series, while Magnesium (Mg) is an s-block element.

Extra Facts:
Actinides are radioactive elements and are used in nuclear energy production. Thorium (Th) is used as fuel in thorium-based nuclear reactors. Important actinides like Uranium (U) and Plutonium (Pu) play a key role in nuclear weapons and energy production. Actinides are also used in medical applications, such as cancer treatment.

☛ What is the first element in the lanthanide series? → Lanthanum (La)
☛ What is the atomic number of Thorium? → 90
☛ Which element is neither an actinide nor a lanthanide? → Magnesium (Mg)
☛ What is the atomic number of Uranium? → 92
question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा तत्व एक्टिनाइड श्रेणी का सदस्य है?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options_hi: ल्यूटीशियम (Lutetium)
थोरियम (Thorium)
मैग्नीशियम (Magnesium)
लैंथेनम (Lanthanum)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है थोरियम (Thorium)

Explanation:
एक्टिनाइड श्रेणी के तत्व वे हैं जिनकी परमाणु संख्या 89 (एक्टिनियम) से 103 (लॉरेंशियम) तक होती है। इन तत्वों में 5f-इलेक्ट्रॉनों को भरने की प्रक्रिया होती है। थोरियम (Thorium) का परमाणु क्रमांक 90 है, जो इसे एक्टिनाइड श्रेणी का सदस्य बनाता है। अन्य विकल्पों में, ल्यूटीशियम (Lutetium) और लैंथेनम (Lanthanum) लैंथेनाइड श्रेणी के सदस्य हैं, जबकि मैग्नीशियम (Magnesium) एक s-ब्लॉक तत्व है।

Extra Facts:
एक्टिनाइड तत्व रेडियोधर्मी होते हैं और इनका उपयोग परमाणु ऊर्जा उत्पादन में किया जाता है। थोरियम (Thorium) का उपयोग थोरियम-आधारित परमाणु रिएक्टरों में ईंधन के रूप में किया जाता है। एक्टिनाइड्स में यूरेनियम (Uranium) और प्लूटोनियम (Plutonium) जैसे महत्वपूर्ण तत्व भी शामिल हैं, जो परमाणु हथियारों और ऊर्जा उत्पादन में प्रमुख भूमिका निभाते हैं।

question:
According to Mendeleev's Periodic Table, which element’s properties matched up remarkably well with eka-aluminium ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Scandium
Gallium
Titanium
Germanium
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gallium

Explanation:
Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table and predicted the properties of undiscovered elements, which he named using the prefix 'eka' (meaning 'one' in Sanskrit). He predicted an element called eka-aluminium, which should have properties similar to aluminium. In 1875, gallium was discovered, and its properties (such as atomic mass, density, oxide formula, etc.) matched remarkably well with Mendeleev's predictions for eka-aluminium. Thus, gallium was identified as the element corresponding to eka-aluminium.

Extra Facts:
☛ Mendeleev also predicted other elements like eka-silicon (germanium) and eka-boron (scandium), which were later discovered.
☛ Gallium (Ga) has an atomic number of 31 and belongs to Group 13 (boron group).
☛ Gallium is used in semiconductors, LEDs, and thermometers.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

☛ What is the atomic number of gallium? → 31
☛ What is Group 13 called in the modern periodic table? → Boron group
☛ In which year did Mendeleev present the periodic table? → 1869
☛ What is the melting point of gallium? → 29.76°C

question:
Which of the following is NOT a halogen gas?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: F
He
Cl
Br
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is He (Helium)

Explanation:
Halogen gases are located in Group 17 of the periodic table and include fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), iodine (I), and astatine (At). These are all non-metals and are highly reactive. Helium (He) is a noble gas located in Group 18 and is chemically inert. Therefore, helium is not a halogen gas.

Extra Facts:
Halogen gases exist as diatomic molecules (F2, Cl2, Br2, I2) in nature. They have a high tendency to gain electrons and react with metals to form salts. Noble gases (helium, neon, argon, etc.) are inert due to their complete valence shells and are used in welding, lighting, and medical imaging.

☛ Give an example of noble gases. → Helium, Neon, Argon
☛ Which group do halogen gases belong to? → Group 17
☛ Which is the lightest noble gas? → Helium
☛ What is the color of fluorine gas? → Pale yellow

question:
What is the atomicity of Chlorine?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Tetra-atomic
Diatomic
Poly-atomic
Monoatomic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Diatomic

Explanation:
The atomicity of Chlorine (Cl) is diatomic, meaning its molecule consists of two atoms bonded together by a covalent bond. Chlorine exists as Cl2 gas, where two chlorine atoms combine to form a stable molecule. This property is also observed in other diatomic elements like hydrogen (H2), nitrogen (N2), and oxygen (O2).

Extra Facts:
1. Atomicity: The number of atoms present in one molecule of an element is called its atomicity.
2. Diatomic Molecules: Molecules composed of two atoms, e.g., H2, O2, N2, Cl2.
3. Chlorine: A reactive halogen used in water purification, disinfection, and plastic manufacturing.

question_hi:
क्लोरीन की परमाणुकता क्या है?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options_hi: चतुष्परमाणुक
द्विपरमाणुक
बहु-परमाणुक
एकपरमाणुक
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है द्विपरमाणुक

Explanation:
क्लोरीन (Cl) की परमाणुकता द्विपरमाणुक (Diatomic) होती है। इसका अर्थ है कि क्लोरीन के अणु दो परमाणुओं से मिलकर बने होते हैं, जो एक सहसंयोजक बंधन द्वारा जुड़े होते हैं। क्लोरीन गैस (Cl2) के रूप में पाई जाती है, जहाँ दो क्लोरीन परमाणु आपस में जुड़कर एक स्थिर अणु बनाते हैं। यह गुण अन्य हैलोजन तत्वों जैसे हाइड्रोजन (H2), नाइट्रोजन (N2), ऑक्सीजन (O2) आदि में भी देखा जाता है।

Extra Facts:
1. परमाणुकता (Atomicity): किसी तत्व के एक अणु में उपस्थित परमाणुओं की संख्या को उसकी परमाणुकता कहते हैं।
2. द्विपरमाणुक अणु: ऐसे अणु जिनमें दो परमाणु होते हैं, जैसे H2, O2, N2, Cl2 आदि।
3. क्लोरीन: यह एक प्रतिक्रियाशील हैलोजन तत्व है जिसका उपयोग जल शुद्धिकरण, कीटाणुशोधन और प्लास्टिक निर्माण में किया जाता है।

question:
What was the symbol Henry Moseley used for denoting atomic number?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: M
U
A
Z
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Z

Explanation:
Henry Moseley used the symbol Z to denote the atomic number. In 1913, through X-ray spectroscopy experiments, Moseley proved that the atomic number of an element corresponds to the number of protons in its nucleus. His work demonstrated that the physical and chemical properties of elements depend on their atomic number, not atomic weight. This discovery played a crucial role in the development of the modern periodic table, arranging elements based on increasing atomic number rather than atomic mass.

Extra Facts:

☛ Mass Number (A) = Number of protons + Number of neutrons

question:
Which property of an element is inversely related to its ionisation energy?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Electronegativity
Atomic mass
Atomic radius
Electron affinity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Atomic radius

Explanation:
Ionisation Energy is the minimum energy required to remove an electron from an atom of an element. It depends on the attractive force between the nucleus and the outermost electrons. When the Atomic Radius increases, the outermost electrons move farther from the nucleus, reducing the attractive force and thus decreasing the ionisation energy. Hence, ionisation energy and atomic radius share an inverse relationship. Other options like Electronegativity and Electron Affinity are directly proportional to ionisation energy, while Atomic Mass has no direct relation to it.

Extra Facts:
1. Ionisation Energy increases from left to right in the Periodic Table and decreases from top to bottom.
2. Noble Gases have the highest ionisation energy due to their stable electronic configuration.
3. Metals have low ionisation energy, so they easily lose electrons to form cations.
4. Hydrogen has an ionisation energy of 1312 kJ/mol, which is the lowest among all elements.

question_hi:

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: वैद्युतीयऋणात्मकता
परमाणु-द्रव्यमान
परमाणु-त्रिज्या
इलेक्ट्रान बन्धुता
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है परमाणु-त्रिज्या

Explanation:
आयनीकरण ऊर्जा (Ionisation Energy) किसी तत्व के परमाणु से एक इलेक्ट्रॉन को निकालने के लिए आवश्यक न्यूनतम ऊर्जा होती है। यह ऊर्जा परमाणु के नाभिक और बाहरी इलेक्ट्रॉनों के बीच आकर्षण बल पर निर्भर करती है। परमाणु-त्रिज्या (Atomic Radius) बढ़ने पर, बाहरी इलेक्ट्रॉन नाभिक से दूर हो जाते हैं, जिससे नाभिक का आकर्षण बल कम हो जाता है और आयनीकरण ऊर्जा कम हो जाती है। इसलिए, आयनीकरण ऊर्जा और परमाणु-त्रिज्या के बीच व्युत्क्रमानुपाती (Inverse) संबंध होता है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे वैद्युतीयऋणात्मकता (Electronegativity) और इलेक्ट्रॉन बन्धुता (Electron Affinity) आयनीकरण ऊर्जा के सीधे आनुपातिक होते हैं, जबकि परमाणु-द्रव्यमान (Atomic Mass) का इससे कोई सीधा संबंध नहीं होता।

2. नोबल गैसों (Noble Gases) की आयनीकरण ऊर्जा सबसे अधिक होती है क्योंकि उनका इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास स्थिर होता है।
3. धातुएं (Metals) की आयनीकरण ऊर्जा कम होती है, इसलिए वे आसानी से इलेक्ट्रॉन त्यागकर धनायन (Cations) बनाती हैं।
4. हाइड्रोजन (Hydrogen) की आयनीकरण ऊर्जा 1312 kJ/mol होती है, जो सबसे कम है।

question:
Which of the following is a 's' block element ?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Scandium
Vanadium
Titanium
Rubidium
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rubidium (Rb)

Explanation:
's' block elements are those whose last electron enters the 's' orbital. In the periodic table, these include Group 1 (alkali metals) and Group 2 (alkaline earth metals). Rubidium (Rb) is an alkali metal in Group 1 with an electronic configuration of [Kr]5s1, making it an 's' block element. The other options—Scandium (Sc), Vanadium (V), and Titanium (Ti)—are 'd' block elements as their last electron enters the 'd' orbital.

Extra Facts:
's' block elements exhibit high electropositivity and low ionization energy, making them highly reactive. Alkali metals (e.g., lithium, sodium, potassium) react vigorously with water to produce hydrogen gas. Their oxides and hydroxides are basic in nature. Rubidium is used in ion engines for spacecraft and specialized glass manufacturing.

question:
Which law, that was proposed in 1811, predicted that the same volume of gases at the same temperature and pressure would have the same number of molecules?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Dalton’s law
Gay-Lussac’s law
Avogadro’s law
Charles' law
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Avogadro’s law

Explanation:
Proposed by Italian scientist Amedeo Avogadro in 1811, Avogadro’s law states that equal volumes of all gases, at the same temperature and pressure, contain the same number of molecules. According to this law, 1 mole of any gas contains 6.022 × 1023 molecules (Avogadro’s number) and occupies 22.4 liters at Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP). This law forms the basis of the ideal gas equation (PV = nRT) and helps determine molecular masses.

Extra Facts:
◉ Avogadro was the first to distinguish between molecules and atoms.
◉ Avogadro’s number (6.022 × 1023) was named in his honor.
◉ The law resolved inconsistencies between Dalton’s atomic theory and Gay-Lussac’s gas combination law.
◉ At STP (0°C, 1 atm), the molar volume of all gases is 22.4 liters.

question:
How many maximum electrons can M shell have?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: 18
8
1
2
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 18

Explanation:
The M shell is the third shell, and its principal quantum number (n) is 3. The maximum number of electrons in any shell is calculated using the formula 2n². According to this formula, the M shell (n=3) can hold a maximum of 2 × (3)² = 2 × 9 = 18 electrons. This formula is based on Bohr's atomic model and quantum mechanical principles. The M shell consists of 3 subshells (s, p, d), which can accommodate 2, 6, and 10 electrons respectively, totaling 18 electrons.

Extra Facts:
☛ Atomic shells are denoted by letters K, L, M, N, etc., where K is the first shell (n=1).
☛ The K shell can hold up to 2 electrons, L shell up to 8, M shell up to 18, and N shell up to 32 electrons.
☛ Subshells (s, p, d, f) can hold s=2, p=6, d=10, and f=14 electrons.
☛ The presence of the d-subshell (n=3, l=2) in the M shell allows it to hold more electrons, whereas the L shell (n=2) only has s and p subshells.

question:
Identify a monoatomic molecule.

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: carbon monoxide
Oxygen
Helium
Chlorine
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Helium

Explanation:
A monoatomic molecule is a molecule composed of only one atom. Helium (He) is an example because it is a noble gas and exists as a single atom in nature. Other options like carbon monoxide (CO), oxygen (O₂), and chlorine (Cl₂) are diatomic molecules as they consist of two atoms bonded together. Noble gases (e.g., helium, neon, argon) are typically monoatomic because their outer electron shells are completely filled, making them chemically inert and unlikely to form bonds with other atoms.

Extra Facts:
Noble Gases: These gases belong to Group 18 of the periodic table and have completely filled outer electron shells, making them inert. Examples include helium (He), neon (Ne), argon (Ar), krypton (Kr), xenon (Xe), and radon (Rn). They are used in welding, lighting (neon lights), and medical imaging (helium in MRI). Helium is also used in balloons due to its low density and non-flammability.

question:
Name the element which has an electronic configuration of 2, 8, 7

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Hydrogen
Helium
Chlorine
Carbon
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chlorine

Explanation:
The element with the electronic configuration 2, 8, 7 has an atomic number of 17, as the total number of electrons (2 + 8 + 7 = 17) equals the atomic number. In the periodic table, the element with atomic number 17 is Chlorine (Cl). Chlorine is a halogen group element with a valency of 1 because it has 7 electrons in its outermost shell and gains one electron to achieve a stable octet. It is a non-metal and exists as a diatomic molecule (Cl2) in nature.

Extra Facts:
Chlorine is a yellow-green gas widely used in water treatment, disinfection, and PVC production. It is found in seawater as sodium chloride (NaCl). Chlorine is a key component of bleaching powder (CaOCl2), used in the textile industry and water purification. The halogen group includes fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), iodine (I), and astatine (At). Chlorine is highly reactive and forms compounds like HCl and NaCl.

A unique characteristic of gallium is that it melts in the palm of the hand, making it useful for various experiments.

Extra Facts:
Gallium was discovered in 1875 by French chemist Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran. It is found in trace amounts in the Earth's crust and is extracted from zinc and aluminum ores. Gallium is also used in medicine, such as the radioisotope gallium-67, which is used to detect tumors and infections. Gallium metal can exist in a liquid state like mercury but is less toxic than mercury.

question:
In the periodic table, what is the trend for atomic radius as you move from left to right across a period (horizontal row)?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Atomic radius remains constant
Atomic radius increases
Atomic radius exhibits irregular behaviour
Atomic radius decreases
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Atomic radius decreases

Explanation:
In the periodic table, as you move from left to right across a period (horizontal row), the atomic radius decreases. This is because, as we move across a period, the atomic number increases, leading to an increase in the number of protons in the nucleus. This results in a greater positive charge in the nucleus, which exerts a stronger attractive force on the electrons. Although electrons are added to the same shell, the increased effective nuclear charge causes the electron cloud to contract, thereby reducing the atomic radius. This explains why the size of atoms decreases from left to right in a period.

Extra Facts:
1. In a group (vertical column) of the periodic table, the atomic radius increases as you move down because new electron shells are added.
2. The smallest atoms are helium (He) and hydrogen (H), while the largest atoms are located at the bottom left corner of the periodic table.
3. Atomic radius is typically measured as half the distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms.

question:
All noble gas molecules are-

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Diatomic
Tri atomic
Polyatomic
Monoatomic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Monoatomic

Explanation:
Noble gases such as Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), and Radon (Rn) exist naturally as monoatomic molecules. Their outermost electron shells are completely filled, making them chemically inert and unreactive with other elements. Due to their stability, they remain as individual atoms and do not form diatomic or polyatomic molecules. Thus, noble gas molecules are monoatomic.

Extra Facts:
Noble gases are also called 'Group 0' elements because their valency is zero. These gases are found in very small quantities in the atmosphere. Helium is used in balloons and meteorology, while Neon is used in neon sign boards. Argon is used in welding and light bulbs. These gases were discovered by Sir William Ramsay.

question:
Which of the following is monoatomic?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Nitrogen
Oxygen
Chlorine
Helium
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Helium (He)

Explanation:
Monoatomic elements are those that exist as single atoms in their natural state. Helium (He) is a noble gas with atomic number 2 and has a stable electronic configuration (1s²), which prevents it from forming bonds with other atoms. Hence, it exists as a monoatomic gas.

Nitrogen (N₂), Oxygen (O₂), and Chlorine (Cl₂) are diatomic molecules, meaning they consist of two atoms bonded together. These elements naturally occur as diatomic molecules under standard conditions.

Extra Facts:
Noble Gases: Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), and Radon (Rn) are all monoatomic gases due to their complete valence shells, making them chemically inert.
Diatomic Molecules: H₂, N₂, O₂, F₂, Cl₂, Br₂, and I₂ are the seven diatomic elements that exist as two-atom molecules in nature.

question:
Each element has a name and ___________.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: a unique colour
a unique shape
a unique chemical symbol
a unique physical symbol
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is a unique chemical symbol

Explanation:
Each element has a name and a unique chemical symbol. Chemical symbols are used internationally to identify elements. These symbols are typically derived from the first letter (or first two letters) of the element's English or Latin name. For example, hydrogen is represented by 'H', oxygen by 'O', and sodium by 'Na' (from Latin 'Natrium'). This system is standardized by IUPAC (International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry). Chemical symbols are used in chemical equations and formulas, making scientific communication simple and universal.

Extra Facts:
The history of chemical symbols dates back to John Dalton, who used pictorial symbols for elements. Later, Berzelius proposed the current letter-based system. The periodic table includes unique symbols for all 118 known elements. Some symbols are derived from Latin names, such as iron (Fe - Ferrum), gold (Au - Aurum), and mercury (Hg - Hydrargyrum). This system is crucial in scientific research and education.

question:
Which scientist invented the Periodic table?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Ernest Rutherford
Dalton

Dmitri Mendeleev
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dmitri Mendeleev

Explanation:
The Periodic Table was invented by the Russian scientist Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869. Mendeleev arranged the elements based on their atomic weights and observed that the properties of elements repeat at regular intervals. This led to the creation of the Periodic Table. Mendeleev left gaps in his table for undiscovered elements, which were later filled by elements like Gallium and Germanium. His table became the foundation for the modern Periodic Table.

Extra Facts:
In the Periodic Table, elements are arranged in periods and groups. The modern Periodic Table organizes elements by their atomic number. The table categorizes elements into metals, non-metals, and metalloids. After Mendeleev, Henry Moseley refined the Periodic Table by introducing the concept of atomic number.

question:

solution:

Explanation:
Carbon is a versatile element that forms the basis for all living organisms and many of the things we use. It is the main component of organic compounds and can form a wide variety of molecules due to its unique ability to form covalent bonds. Carbon shares four electrons to create stable compounds, a property known as tetravalency. It is the fundamental building block of hydrocarbons, proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids, etc., which are essential for life. Additionally, carbon forms important materials like diamond, graphite, and coal.

Extra Facts:
Carbon has an atomic number of 6 and belongs to Group 14. Its allotropes include diamond (the hardest natural substance), graphite (a conductor of electricity), and fullerenes (nanotubes). The study of carbon compounds is known as organic chemistry. Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a crucial component of the atmosphere and plays a vital role in photosynthesis. Carbon compounds are used in the production of medicines, plastics, fuels, textiles, etc.

options_hi: क्यूरियम
बेरियम
एंटीमनी
कार्बन
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कार्बन

Explanation:
कार्बन एक बहुमुखी तत्व है जो सभी जीवित जीवों और हमारे द्वारा उपयोग की जाने वाली कई चीजों का आधार बनता है। यह जैविक यौगिकों (Organic Compounds) का मुख्य घटक है और कोवैलेंट बंध (Covalent Bond) बनाने की अपनी अद्वितीय क्षमता के कारण विभिन्न प्रकार के अणुओं का निर्माण कर सकता है। कार्बन चार इलेक्ट्रॉनों को साझा करके स्थिर यौगिक बनाता है, जिसे टेट्रावैलेंसी (Tetravalency) कहा जाता है। यह हाइड्रोकार्बन, प्रोटीन, कार्बोहाइड्रेट, लिपिड, न्यूक्लिक एसिड आदि का मूल घटक है, जो जीवन के लिए आवश्यक हैं। इसके अलावा, कार्बन हीरा, ग्रेफाइट, कोयला जैसे महत्वपूर्ण पदार्थों का भी निर्माण करता है।

Extra Facts:
कार्बन का परमाणु क्रमांक 6 है और यह समूह 14 का सदस्य है। कार्बन के अपरूप (Allotropes) में हीरा (सबसे कठोर प्राकृतिक पदार्थ), ग्रेफाइट (विद्युत का सुचालक), और फुलरीन (नैनोट्यूब) शामिल हैं। कार्बन यौगिकों का अध्ययन कार्बनिक रसायन (Organic Chemistry) में किया जाता है। कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड (CO2) वायुमंडल का एक महत्वपूर्ण घटक है और प्रकाश संश्लेषण (Photosynthesis) में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। कार्बन यौगिकों का उपयोग दवाओं, प्लास्टिक, ईंधन, कपड़ों आदि के निर्माण में किया जाता है।

question:
Which of the following elements is a part of the P block of the periodic table?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Rhodium
Hydrogen
Oxygen
Silver
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Oxygen

Explanation:
In the periodic table, elements are divided into s, p, d, and f blocks. The elements of the P block have their outermost electrons entering the p-orbital. Oxygen (O) has an atomic number of 8 and its electronic configuration is 1s² 2s² 2p⁴, where the last electron enters the 2p orbital. Hence, it is a P block element. Among the other options, Rhodium (Rh) and Silver (Ag) are d block elements, while Hydrogen (H) is an s block element.

Extra Facts:
The P block includes elements from groups 13 to 18, encompassing metals, non-metals, and metalloids. This block contains elements with diverse properties, such as noble gases, halogens, and other significant elements. P block elements are widely used in daily life, e.g., Oxygen (O) is essential for respiration, Nitrogen (N) is a major component of the atmosphere, and Carbon (C) is the basis of organic compounds.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा तत्व आवर्त सारणी के P ब्लॉक का हिस्सा है?

[SSC GD 2024]
options_hi: रोडियाम (Rhodium)
हाइड्रोजन (Hydrogen
ऑक्सीजन (Oxygen)
सिल्वर (Silver)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है ऑक्सीजन (Oxygen)

Explanation:
आवर्त सारणी में तत्वों को s, p, d और f ब्लॉक में विभाजित किया गया है। P ब्लॉक के तत्वों का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास उनके अंतिम इलेक्ट्रॉन के p-ऑर्बिटल में प्रवेश करने से पूरा होता है। ऑक्सीजन (O) का परमाणु क्रमांक 8 है और इसका इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास 1s² 2s² 2p⁴ है, जिसमें अंतिम इलेक्ट्रॉन 2p ऑर्बिटल में प्रवेश करता है। इसलिए, यह P ब्लॉक का तत्व है। अन्य विकल्पों में, रोडियाम (Rh) और सिल्वर (Ag) d ब्लॉक के तत्व हैं, जबकि हाइड्रोजन (H) s ब्लॉक का तत्व है।

Extra Facts:
P ब्लॉक में समूह 13 से 18 के तत्व शामिल हैं, जिनमें धातु, अधातु और उपधातु सभी शामिल हैं। यह ब्लॉक विविध गुणों वाले तत्वों को शामिल करता है, जैसे कि अक्रिय गैसें (नोबल गैसें), हैलोजन और अन्य महत्वपूर्ण तत्व। P ब्लॉक के तत्वों का उपयोग दैनिक जीवन में व्यापक रूप से किया जाता है, जैसे कि ऑक्सीजन (O) श्वसन के लिए आवश्यक है, नाइट्रोजन (N) वायुमंडल का प्रमुख घटक है, और कार्बन (C) कार्बनिक यौगिकों का आधार है।
